Braised Chicken Legs with Rice, Potatoes & Veggies🍗 Ingredients * 1 package chicken drumsticks (6–7 pieces) * 1-2 tbsp olive oil * 1 tsp salt * 1 tsp black pepper * 2 tsp garlic powder * 2 tsp onion powder * 2 tsp paprika * ½ tsp cumin * 1 jalapeño, diced * ½ red onion, diced * 1 tbsp sun-dried tomato paste * 1 tbsp @Loisa sofrito * 5–6 garlic cloves, minced * 4 cups chicken stock * 1 (8 oz) can tomato sauce * Small potatoes, halved (about 10–12 baby potatoes) * 1 zucchini, diced * Cooked white rice, for serving (let me know if you guys want my rice recipe) Instructions: 1. Clean the chicken with vinegar, then pat completely dry with paper towels. 2. Season the chicken with the salt, pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, and cumin. Toss until evenly coated. 3. Heat the olive oil in a large Dutch oven or deep skillet over medium-high heat. 4. Brown the chicken for 2–3 minutes per side until golden. It doesn’t need to be cooked through. Remove and set aside. 5. In the same pot, add the diced jalapeño and red onion. Cook for about 5 minutes until softened. 6. Stir in the sun-dried tomato paste and cook for 30 seconds. 7. Add the Loisa Sofrito and minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. 8. Pour in the chicken stock and tomato sauce, stirring to combine. Bring to a gentle boil. 9. Return the chicken to the pot. Reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for about 1 hour, or until the chicken is fall-apart tender and the sauce has reduced. 10. About 20 minutes before the chicken is done, add the halved potatoes and diced zucchini. Continue simmering until the potatoes are fork-tender and the zucchini is cooked. 11. Serve over fluffy white rice and spoon plenty of the sauce over the top. #chickenlegs #braised #onepotmeals #cookwithme

EASY MEALS FOR 2 EP 22 Crispy Gochujang Chicken Thighs Ingredients Really a meal for 1 because someone ate all of it :)  Chicken * 400–450 g boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces * 1/2 teaspoon salt * 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder * 1/2 teaspoon black pepper * 3 tablespoons cornstarch * 3–4 tablespoons neutral oil, for shallow-frying, enough to cover bottom of pan  Spicy gochujang sauce * 1 tbsp butter  * 1½ tablespoons gochujang * 1 tablespoon soy sauce * 1 tablespoon brown sugar * 1 tablespoon rice vinegar * 2 teaspoons sesame oil * 3 cloves garlic, finely minced * 1 teaspoon grated ginger * 1/4 cup water For serving * Steamed rice * Sliced green onion * Toasted sesame seeds * Cucumber, optional Instructions 1. Pat the chicken thighs dry and cut them into bite-sized pieces. Season with salt, garlic powder, black pepper. 2. Add the cornstarch and toss until the chicken is evenly coated with a thin, dry layer. 3. Heat the neutral oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the chicken in a single layer and shallow-fry for 4–5 minutes per side, or until golden, crispy and cooked through. Work in batches if necessary. 4. Transfer the chicken to a plate. Carefully remove the oil, add butter to skillet. 5. Reduce the heat to medium-low. Add the garlic and ginger and cook for about 30 seconds. 6. Stir in the gochujang, soy sauce, honey, rice vinegar, sesame oil, water and optional gochugaru. Simmer for 1–2 minutes, stirring, until glossy and slightly thickened. 7. Return the chicken to the skillet and toss for 30–60 seconds, until evenly coated. Don’t cook it in the sauce for too long or the coating will soften. 8. top 5 tips to start your healthy hair care journey🌱✨ 1. cut off those split ends✂️      split ends can’t be repaired, only temporarily sealed. if you leave them, they can continue splitting farther up the hair shaft, leading to more breakage over time. regular trims help keep your hair looking thicker and healthier while preventing you from losing more length later. 2. do a 10 minute scalp massage daily💆🏼‍♀️      your scalp is skin, and healthy hair starts there. daily scalp massages can help increase blood flow to the scalp, reduce buildup, and create a healthier environment for your hair to grow. you can use your fingertips or a scalp massager. just be gentle and consistent. 3. start scalp + hair oiling🫶      find the right hair oil for your scalp and hair type because not every oil works for everyone. i oil my scalp for density, not to make my hair grow faster. massage it in for a few minutes 1 to 3 times a week before wash day, then wash it out after 3 to 4 hours if your scalp tolerates it well. i also have other videos that go into all the do’s and don’ts of hair oiling if you want to learn more. 4. get a blood panel done🩸      if your hair feels thinner than normal, sheds excessively, or isn’t growing like it used to, it may be worth asking your doctor for blood work. things like low iron, vitamin d, b12, zinc, or other deficiencies can affect hair health. if you’re deficient, focus on vitamin rich foods and only take supplements if recommended by your healthcare provider. 5. learn your hair before buying products🤍      figure out your hair pattern (straight, wavy, curly, or coily), strand texture (fine, medium, or coarse), porosity (how well your hair absorbs and holds moisture), and scalp type (oily, dry, balanced, or sensitive). once you know those, it’s much easier to build a routine that actually works for you instead of wasting money on products that aren’t a good fit. healthy hair isn’t about buying the most expensive products. it’s about understanding your hair, staying consistent, and being patient. 🤍   #haircare #healthyhair #HairCareTips #kayliboyle

not all hair care has to break you bank💰 1. brush starting at your ends and work your way up -starting at your ends helps remove tangles little by little instead of pulling one big knot through your entire strand. this puts a lot less tension on your hair, helps prevent unnecessary breakage, and is especially important if your hair is fine or prone to tangling. 2. scalp massages -i like to do a 5 to 10 minute scalp massage every day. this can help increase blood flow to the scalp, helps distribute your natural oils, and feels amazing. i personally do it because it’s great for overall scalp health and can support healthier, denser hair over time.  3. never sleep with wet hair -wet hair is at its weakest, so tossing and turning on a pillow all night creates extra friction that can lead to breakage, frizz, and split ends. it may seem convenient but in the long run it causes so much damage.  4. always split and rinse your hair after shampoo and conditioner -don’t just let the water run over the top of your head. separate your hair into sections and make sure you’re rinsing all the way down to your scalp and underneath your hair. leftover shampoo or conditioner can cause buildup, weigh your hair down, and even contribute to an itchy or irritated scalp. 5. wear protective hairstyles -protective styles help reduce friction, tangles, and unnecessary breakage throughout the day. i usually wear a very loose claw clip updo or a loose french braid. the key is keeping them loose, not tight. if your hairstyle is pulling on your scalp, it’s too tight. healthy hair isn’t about finding one miracle product. it’s all the little habits you stay consistent with that make the biggest difference over time💪🏻    #hair #haircare #healthyhair  #hairtips #kayliboyle
